title: A representing cocone for the stage pullback Hom functors
statement: Let I be a preorder, R:I→CommRing a ring diagram, c a cocone and i∈I. Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with s:Y→Spec(R_i). Assume fixed-universe derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] for every scheme and for each localized module site on an open of Y. For Q∈D(O_Y) perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], there are F:tail(≥i)→D(O_Y) and a cocone d. Each F_j and d.pt has quasi-coherent cohomology. There are equivalences e_j,M:Hom(M,F_j)≃Hom(Lpi_j* M,Lpi_j* Q) and b_M:Hom(M,d.pt)≃Hom(Lpi_inf* M,Lpi_inf* Q) for every M∈D(O_Y), where pi_j:Y×Spec(R_j)→Y and pi_inf:Y×Spec(c.pt)→Y are the projections. Both are natural under precomposition: e_j,M(g∘f)=Lpi_j*(g)∘e_j,N(f), and similarly for b. Postcomposition with F(j≤k) corresponds to perfectStageMap, and postcomposition with d_j corresponds to perfectLimitMap [lem-pc-perfect-hom-transport]. PerfectHomPushPullData packages exactly these quasi-coherence, equivalence, naturality and transport clauses; it is constructed from given data, not from an existence witness. No triangles, covers, group colimits, directedness, finite presentation or IsColimit(c) are asserted or required.

proof.text: At each stage take B_j=Rpi_j*Lpi_j*Q and at the limit take B_inf=Rpi_inf*Lpi_inf*Q. The derived adjunction gives e and b, naturally in M.

Naturality of perfectHomComparison in the testing object gives naturality of perfectStageMap and perfectLimitMap under precomposition. Conjugate by e and b and evaluate at the identity of B_j to construct representing transition maps and cocone legs. Naturality at f:M→B_j gives f followed by the representing arrow equals the conjugated transport of f.

The identity equation is read from perfect_hom_stage_colimit at an identity arrow. perfectHomMap_trans gives composition; perfectLimitMap_stage gives cocone compatibility. Applying the injective adjunction equivalences verifies the functor and cocone laws and their pinning equations.

Perfect Q has quasi-coherent cohomology. Derived pullback preserves it. Both projections are affine, hence qcqs; their derived direct images preserve quasi-coherent cohomology. This proves the two quasi-coherence fields.
